messages:
oncall-bot: Pager: HIGH severity — cross-region routing anomalies detected for latency-steering policy (route: steer-eu-us). See metrics: https://prom.redwood/graph/ABCD :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: Incident channel created: #incidents — thread started

alex: seeing elevated 502s from eu requests since ~07:12 UTC. Also huge tail latency for some requests (p95->3.1s). Customers in eu-west1 complaining.

sam: confirming. 5xx rate from eu cluster up ~18% over baseline. Traces show requests are being routed to us-central1 due to what looks like a steering decision flip.

kavita: any recent config deploys to steering service? I don't see a rollout in the last 24h.

cloud-svcs: there's a surge of stale health metrics on the metrics aggregator between 07:08-07:14 — some health checks from eu-west1 were delayed and marked unhealthy briefly. Latency steering uses those aggregated latencies for region selection.

alex: that would explain it — if eu looked unhealthy steering could send traffic to us where latency is higher and cause user-visible errors.

sam: grabbing logs from steer-proxy: ```
2026-03-15T07:11:29Z steer-proxy INFO evaluate_policy request_id=abcd region_scores={eu: 120, us: 80} metric_age_ms=54000
2026-03-15T07:11:29Z steer-proxy WARN metric_age_above_threshold region=eu age_ms=54000
2026-03-15T07:11:30Z steer-proxy ACTION route_override from=eu to=us reason=metric_age
```

alex: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable latency-steering feature flag 2) pin eu traffic to eu fallback pool 3) force-refresh health metrics aggregator. Prefer 2+3 to minimize churn. Thoughts?

kavita: agree with 2+3. Disabling steering is heavier and could ripple. Pinning should be quick: `curl -XPOST https://control.redwood/pin -d '{"policy":"steer-eu-us","pin_region":"eu-west1","ttl":300}'` (will require ops token).

mei: I'm taking the pin action now and simultaneously kicking off a metrics aggregator refresh. @sam can you validate after pin? I'll also set TTL low to allow safe rollback.

mei: (running) ```
> curl -XPOST https://control.redwood/pin -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"policy":"steer-eu-us","pin_region":"eu-west1","ttl":300}'
200 OK
{"result":"pinned","policy":"steer-eu-us","region":"eu-west1","expires_in":300}
```

sam: seeing route decisions flip back to eu within 20s. 5xx rate dropping toward baseline, p95 latency moving down. Nice.

incident-coordinator: customer impact estimate: approx 11:06-07:18 UTC window saw ~12% of prod requests for eu routed off-region, error budget burn ~3.2%, ~4 high-severity customer support tickets so far. Roll forward mitigation reduced impact by 80%.

alex: good mitigation. Next steps: 1) investigate why metrics aggregator flagged eu health metrics as stale (logs/ingest lag) 2) add alert for metric staleness per-region 3) postmortem and follow-up for steering fail-safe (auto-fallback to pin when metric_age > X).

cloud-svcs: initial root cause: a partial GC spike on metrics-agg pod set caused ingestion lag for ~45s, causing metric_age to exceed steering threshold. I've redeployed a tuned metrics-agg image (v2.4.1-rc) to reduce GC pauses and increased retention of recent samples.

sam: I've created a temporary playbook entry in runbook: "steering-metric-staleness" with commands for pinning and forcing aggregator refresh. Adding runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/steering-metric-staleness

mei: handing off to @alex (next oncall) in 10m for post-incident cleanup and monitoring. I'll remain available.

alex: taking over. I'll keep the pin for another 5m while we watch, then TTL -> 0 (unpin) once steady. Also opening a postmortem ticket and scheduling follow-up with metrics + steering team.

incident-coordinator: notes for postmortem: timeline, customer impact, mitigation steps, root cause GC issue, fixes deployed, and action items: alert for metric_age, steering auto-pin fallback, improve metrics-agg observability.

oncall-bot: Incident severity -> P2 (customer-impacting, mitigated). Creating incident record #INC-2026-0412.

alex: quick status update in 15m with final numbers. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
